# Job Chapter 30 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 427r–427v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/JOB_030_page_001.jpg, JOB_030_page_002.jpg

---

**1** "But now I am mocked by men younger than I am — men whose fathers I considered beneath the dogs that guard my sheep.

**2** What use was the strength of their hands to me? Their vigor had completely drained away.

**3** Gaunt from poverty and hunger, they gnaw the dry, desolate wasteland in the dead of night.

**4** They pick saltwort from the bushes and eat the roots of broom plants.

**5** They are driven away from other people; everyone shouts at them as if they were thieves.

**6** They are forced to live in the gullies of dried-up streams, in caves and among the rocks.

**7** They howl among the bushes and huddle together under the thorns —

**8** a worthless, nameless brood, driven out of the land with whips.

**9** And now their sons make up songs to mock me; I have become their punchline.

**10** They detest me and keep their distance; they do not hesitate to spit in my face.

**11** Because God has stripped me of my strength and brought me low, they feel free to attack me without restraint.

**12** On my right side a mob rises up; they trip my feet and build their siege ramps against me.

**13** They tear up my road, and they profit from my disaster — with no one to stop them.

**14** They pour through the breach like floodwater; they come crashing in amid the rubble.

**15** Terror overwhelms me; my dignity is blown away like wind, and my security vanishes like a cloud.

**16** And now my life ebbs away; days of suffering have seized me.

**17** Night pierces my bones with pain; the gnawing ache never rests.

**18** God seizes my clothing with violent force, gripping me by the collar of my shirt.

**19** He has thrown me into the mud, and I am reduced to dust and ashes.

**20** I cry out to you, God, but you do not answer! I stand before you, but you just stare at me!

**21** You have become cruel to me; you use your mighty hand to persecute me.

**22** You snatch me up in the wind and toss me around in the storm until I am undone.

**23** I know that you are bringing me to death — to the place where every living person must go.

**24** Surely no one would strike a person who is already in ruins? Surely one cries for help when disaster hits?

**25** Did I not weep for those going through hard times? Did my heart not grieve for the poor?

**26** Yet when I expected good, evil came instead; when I looked for light, only darkness arrived.

**27** My gut churns without relief; days of suffering confront me at every turn.

**28** I wander about in gloom — but not from an eclipse; I stand up in the assembly and cry for help.

**29** I have become a brother to jackals and a companion to owls.

**30** My skin blackens and peels off; my bones burn with fever.

**31** My harp plays only funeral songs now, and my flute sounds only the notes of weeping."

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**The architecture of despair:** Chapter 30 is the mirror image of chapter 29. Every element of Job's former glory has its exact opposite here: respect becomes mockery (vv.1-10), honor becomes disgrace (v.15), God's friendship becomes God's cruelty (vv.19-22), and music becomes mourning (v.31).

**v.20 — The unanswered cry:** This is the most anguished verse in the chapter. Job cries and God does not answer. He stands and God merely stares. The God who once held "intimate friendship" with Job (29:4) has become a cold, silent observer.

**v.26 — The problem of Job in one verse:** "I expected good, evil came; I looked for light, only darkness arrived." This is the Book of Job's thesis in miniature. If the retribution principle were true, Job's good life should have continued. It did not.

*— PNEUMA*
